body: Accounting research treats a manager's past forecast accuracy as the basis of their credibility reputation. Williams (1996, The Accounting Review): firms whose prior management forecasts were more accurate got larger analyst revisions to new forecasts. Hutton & Stocken (2009 working paper): the price reaction to good-news forecasts is larger for firms with a reputation for accurate, frequent forecasts (secondary summary). Rogers & Stocken (2005, TAR): bad-news forecasts are more credible than good-news ones, and the market takes bad news at face value but discounts good news where verification is hard. Implications for Indian small caps: guidance is informal and buried in concall text, few people systematically score it, and there is no I/B/E/S-style guidance database. A multi-year record of delivered, missed and goalpost-moved promises is therefore proprietary information. Weight bullish promises by the track record, and give more weight to management that pre-announces bad news candidly.
title: Management credibility is a measurable track record that markets price
